extra.message: User-controlled 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into an os.system() call: _os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands via the host parameter (e.g., '; cat /etc/passwd').

User-controlled 'expr' query parameter is passed directly to eval(): eval(expr, {"__builtins__": {}}, {"amount": 42, "fee": 7}). Even with __builtins__ disabled, eval() can be exploited for arbitrary code execution through Python object introspection.

User-controlled 'url' query parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen() without validation. An attacker can make the server send requests to arbitrary internal or external URLs, including internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, etc.

User-controlled 'packet_ref' query parameter is used to construct a file path via pathlib Path: parcel_path = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref. No sanitization or path validation is performed. An attacker can use '../' sequences to read arbitrary files on the filesystem (e.g., packet_ref=../../etc/passwd).

User-controlled 'name' query parameter is used to construct a file write path: target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name. An attacker can use '../' sequences to write arbitrary files anywhere on the filesystem (e.g., name=../../app/main.py to overwrite application code).
User-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse(lane). An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to any arbitrary external domain, enabling phishing attacks.

User-controlled 'card' query parameter is rendered in a Jinja2 template with the |safe filter, which disables HTML auto-escaping: Template("{{ card|safe }}").render(card=card). The result is returned as HTMLResponse, allowing cross-site scripting.

User-controlled 'fragment' query parameter is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string: Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). An attacker can inject Jinja2 expressions like {{ config }} or {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} to achieve remote code execution. The result is returned as HTMLResponse, also enabling XSS.

The Origin request header value is reflected directly into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials set to true. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the application, bypassing the Same-Origin Policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: XSS protection and Content Security Policy are explicitly disabled: response.headers["X-XSS-Protection"] = "0" and response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = "". This removes browser-level defenses against XSS attacks.

User-controlled JSON payload is used directly as a MongoDB query filter: MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g., {"$gt": ""}) to bypass filters and extract unauthorized data.

XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, enabling XML External Entity processing. An attacker can send crafted XML with external entity references to read arbitrary files or perform SSRF.
SSL certificate verification is disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context(). This allows man-in-the-middle attacks when connecting to the partner endpoint.

User-controlled 'marker' query parameter is set as a cookie value without validation or sanitization: response.set_cookie("portal_crumb", marker). An attacker can inject arbitrary cookie values including special characters that could enable HTTP header injection.

cwe: CWE-644: HTTP Header Injection via CRLF

extra.message: User-controlled JSON payload is directly used to update a dictionary containing security-sensitive properties (role, tier, approved, balance) via workset.update(payload). An attacker can overwrite any property, including security-critical ones like approved=True or role=admin.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The /api/integrations/webhook/receive endpoint has no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can POST data to this endpoint, which could be abused for denial of service or to exploit downstream processing.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /api/integrations/status/{app_id} endpoint has no authentication. Any unauthenticated user can query the status of any loan application by ID, exposing sensitive business data. This also constitutes an IDOR vulnerability since sequential application IDs can be enumerated.

A hardcoded default SECRET_KEY 'change-me-in-production-32-char-long-key' is used for JWT token signing. If the environment variable is not set, this known key can be used to forge arbitrary JWT tokens and impersonate any user.

A hardcoded default DATABASE_URL containing credentials 'postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/fintech_lending' is used. If the environment variable is not set, these known database credentials can be used to access the database.

The access_token cookie is set with secure=False, meaning it will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. An attacker on the network can intercept the session token via HTTP, leading to session hijacking.

The uploads directory is mounted as static files at /uploads without any authentication. In a fintech lending application, uploaded documents contain highly sensitive personal and financial data (SSNs, bank statements, tax returns). Any unauthenticated user can access these documents by guessing file paths.

Social Security Numbers (SSN) of business owners are exposed in the API response: "ssn": o.ssn. SSNs are highly sensitive PII and should never be returned in full in API responses. They should be masked or omitted entirely.

Hardcoded credential verifier values in the identity endpoint: known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}. These act as shared secrets for authentication and are embedded in source code, which is accessible to anyone with code access.
